```{r}
# Load libraries
#install.packages(c("tidyverse", "janitor", "DataExplorer", "GGally", "naniar", "ggthemes"))
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(DataExplorer)
library(GGally)
library(naniar)
library(ggthemes)

# Step 1: Clean column names (optional but recommended)
obesity <- obesity %>% clean_names()

# Step 2: Check structure and first few rows
str(obesity)
head(obesity)

# Step 3: Plot outcome variable distribution
obesity$n_obeyesdad <- as.factor(obesity$n_obeyesdad)  # if not already a factor

ggplot(obesity, aes(x = fct_infreq(n_obeyesdad))) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#4C72B0") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Obesity Level Distribution", x = "Obesity Category", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# Step 4: Categorical variables distribution
#cat_vars <- obesity %>% select(where(is.character), where(is.factor))
cat_vars <- c("gender", "family_history_with_overweight", "favc", "caec",
              "smoke", "scc", "calc", "mtrans", "n_obeyesdad")


library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

# Frequency tables and percentages for categorical variables
for (var in cat_vars) {
  cat("\n============================\n")
  cat("Variable:", var, "\n\n")
  
  freq_tbl <- obesity %>%
    count(!!sym(var)) %>%
    mutate(percent = n / sum(n) * 100)
  
  print(freq_tbl)
}

# Bar plots for categorical variables
for (var in cat_vars) {
  print(
    ggplot(obesity, aes_string(x = var)) +
      geom_bar(fill = "#55A868") +
      coord_flip() +
      labs(title = paste("Distribution of", var),
           x = var,
           y = "Count") +
      theme_minimal()
  )
}

# Cross-tabulation of each categorical variable with obesity level
for (var in setdiff(cat_vars, "n_obeyesdad")) {
  cat("\n============================\n")
  cat("Cross-tabulation:", var, "vs n_obeyesdad\n\n")
  
  tab <- obesity %>%
    tabyl(!!sym(var), n_obeyesdad) %>%
    adorn_percentages("row") %>%
    adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 1) %>%
    adorn_ns(position = "front")
  
  print(tab)
}



# Step 5: Numeric variable distributions
num_vars <- obesity %>% select(where(is.numeric))

num_vars %>%
  pivot_longer(everything()) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "#C44E52", bins = 30, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Numeric Variables", x = "", y = "Frequency")

# Step 6: Boxplots of numeric variables by obesity category
num_vars_names <- names(num_vars)

for (var in num_vars_names) {
  print(
    ggplot(obesity, aes(x = n_obeyesdad, y = .data[[var]], fill = n_obeyesdad)) +
      geom_boxplot() +
      labs(title = paste("Boxplot of", var, "by Obesity Category"), x = "", y = var) +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
      guides(fill = "none")
  )
}

# Step 7: Correlation matrix for numeric variables
cor_matrix <- cor(num_vars, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

GGally::ggcorr(num_vars, label = TRUE, label_size = 3, hjust = 0.75) +
  ggtitle("Correlation Matrix of Numeric Variables")

# Step 8: Automated EDA report (optional but helpful)
create_report(obesity, y = "n_obeyesdad")
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Make sure your factor variables are factors:
factor_vars <- c("gender", "family_history_with_overweight", "favc", "caec", "smoke",
                 "scc", "calc", "mtrans", "n_obeyesdad")

obesity <- obesity %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(factor_vars), as.factor))

# 1. Obesity level distribution
ggplot(obesity, aes(x = n_obeyesdad)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Obesity Levels", x = "Obesity Level", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# 2. Categorical variables distribution by obesity level
cat_vars <- factor_vars[factor_vars != "n_obeyesdad"]

for (var in cat_vars) {
  print(
    ggplot(obesity, aes_string(x = var, fill = "n_obeyesdad")) +
      geom_bar(position = "fill") +
      labs(title = paste("Proportion of", var, "by Obesity Level"), y = "Proportion") +
      theme_minimal() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  )
}

# 3. Numeric variables distribution by obesity level
num_vars <- c("age", "fcvc", "ncp", "ch2o", "faf", "tue")

for (var in num_vars) {
  print(
    ggplot(obesity, aes_string(x = "n_obeyesdad", y = var)) +
      geom_boxplot(aes(fill = n_obeyesdad)) +

      theme_minimal() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
      guides(fill = "none")
  )
}
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Calculate BMI
obesity <- obesity %>%
  mutate(BMI = weight / (height^2))

# Summary of BMI
summary(obesity$BMI)

# Histogram of BMI
ggplot(obesity, aes(x = BMI)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of BMI", x = "BMI", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# Create BMI categories (standard WHO cutoffs)
obesity <- obesity %>%
  mutate(BMI_category = case_when(
    BMI < 18.5 ~ "Underweight",
    BMI >= 18.5 & BMI < 25 ~ "Normal weight",
    BMI >= 25 & BMI < 30 ~ "Overweight",
    BMI >= 30 ~ "Obese",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  mutate(BMI_category = factor(BMI_category, levels = c("Underweight", "Normal weight", "Overweight", "Obese")))

# Bar plot of BMI categories
ggplot(obesity, aes(x = BMI_category)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "coral") +
  labs(title = "BMI Category Distribution", x = "BMI Category", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# Boxplot of BMI by obesity level
ggplot(obesity, aes(x = n_obeyesdad, y = BMI)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = n_obeyesdad)) +
  labs(title = "BMI by Obesity Level", x = "Obesity Level", y = "BMI") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  guides(fill = "none")
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(obesity, aes(x = age, y = BMI, color = n_obeyesdad)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE) +   # Adds a smooth trend line per obesity level
  labs(
    title = "BMI vs Age by Obesity Level",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "BMI",
    color = "Obesity Level"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

```

```{r}
  tbl <- table(obesity[[var]], obesity$n_obeyesdad)

  cat("\n-------------------------\n")
}
```

```{r}
# Model family history

                 data = obesity, family = binomial)
summary(model_fam)

# Model smoking
model_smoke <- glm(obese_binary ~ smoke + age + gender,
                   data = obesity, family = binomial)
summary(model_smoke)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# --- MCAR: Missing Completely at Random ---
introduce_mcar <- function(data, var, prop_missing) {
  df <- data
  n <- nrow(df)
  missing_indices <- sample(1:n, size = floor(prop_missing * n), replace = FALSE)
  df[missing_indices, var] <- NA
  return(df)
}

# --- MAR: Missing At Random ---
# Missingness in 'var' depends on observed 'dep_var' satisfying a condition
introduce_mar <- function(data, var, dep_var, condition_func, prop_missing) {
  df <- data
  eligible <- which(condition_func(df[[dep_var]]))
  n_miss <- floor(prop_missing * length(eligible))
  if (n_miss == 0) return(df)
  missing_indices <- sample(eligible, size = n_miss, replace = FALSE)
  df[missing_indices, var] <- NA
  return(df)
}

# --- MNAR: Missing Not At Random ---
# Missingness depends on 'var' values themselves (e.g. only for some levels/values)
introduce_mnar <- function(data, var, missing_values, prop_missing) {
  df <- data
  eligible <- which(df[[var]] %in% missing_values)
  n_miss <- floor(prop_missing * length(eligible))
  if (n_miss == 0) return(df)
  missing_indices <- sample(eligible, size = n_miss, replace = FALSE)
  df[missing_indices, var] <- NA
  return(df)
}

# MCAR: 15% missing completely at random in 'favc'
obesity_mcar <- introduce_mcar(obesity, var = "favc", prop_missing = 0.15)

# MAR: Missing 'fcvc' values where age > 30 (30% missing among those)
obesity_mar <- introduce_mar(obesity, var = "fcvc", dep_var = "age",
                            condition_func = function(x) x > 30,
                            prop_missing = 0.3)

# MNAR: Missing 'favc' only for 'yes' values, 40% missingness within that group
obesity_mnar <- introduce_mnar(obesity, var = "favc", missing_values = "yes", prop_missing = 0.4)

```

```{r}
introduce_missing_multiple <- function(data, missing_plan) {
  df <- data
  for (plan in missing_plan) {
    var <- plan$var
    mech <- plan$mechanism
    prop <- plan$prop_missing
    
    if (mech == "MCAR") {
      n <- nrow(df)
      missing_indices <- sample(1:n, size = floor(prop * n), replace = FALSE)
      df[missing_indices, var] <- NA
      
    } else if (mech == "MAR") {
      dep_var <- plan$dep_var
      condition_func <- plan$condition_func
      eligible <- which(condition_func(df[[dep_var]]))
      n_miss <- floor(prop * length(eligible))
      if (n_miss > 0) {
        missing_indices <- sample(eligible, size = n_miss, replace = FALSE)
        df[missing_indices, var] <- NA
      }
      
    } else if (mech == "MNAR") {
      missing_values <- plan$missing_values
      eligible <- which(df[[var]] %in% missing_values)
      n_miss <- floor(prop * length(eligible))
      if (n_miss > 0) {
        missing_indices <- sample(eligible, size = n_miss, replace = FALSE)
        df[missing_indices, var] <- NA
      }
      
    } else {
      stop("Unknown missingness mechanism")
    }
  }
  return(df)
}
missing_plan <- list(
  list(var = "favc", mechanism = "MCAR", prop_missing = 0.15),
  list(var = "fcvc", mechanism = "MAR", prop_missing = 0.25, 
       dep_var = "age", condition_func = function(x) x > 30),
  list(var = "family_history_with_overweight", mechanism = "MNAR", prop_missing = 0.3,
       missing_values = "yes")
)

obesity_missing <- introduce_missing_multiple(obesity, missing_plan)

```
